name: King of Arad
overview: The King of Arad was a male ruler identified as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. While his tribal affiliation is not recorded, he is noted specifically in Joshua 12:14 as a defeated king, possibly the same individual as another king of Arad mentioned elsewhere. There are no additional personal details or notes about him in Scripture beyond this military context.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Arad' directly refers to his role as the monarch over the city or region of Arad. The name itself means 'king of Arad' and does not carry a unique Hebrew or Greek meaning beyond this straightforward designation. This title was not given by God but is a descriptive title used in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Arad beyond what is mentioned in his identification as a king defeated by Joshua. There are no known relatives or tribal connections listed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Arad's significance lies in his defeat by Joshua, which marks the fulfillment of God's promise to give Israel victory over the Canaanite kings. His inclusion among the thirty-one kings conquered demonstrates God's sovereign hand in establishing Israel in the Promised Land. This defeat also reflects the judgment upon the inhabitants of Canaan and the faithfulness of Israel's leadership under Joshua.
